analysis.title: 2027 Global Credit Outlook: Fading Tailwinds and a Growing AI Divide
key_insights: GS expects modest spread widening across USD and EUR IG and HY in 2027. Widening should be gradual in USD and more front-loaded in EUR during 1H2027, reflecting a busy election calendar, energy risks and a weaker technical backdrop.

GS calls the 2027 market 'three-speed' rather than broadly disrupted. AI-related issuers see episodic widening as jumbo deals test absorption capacity, non-AI issuers stay range-bound, and the leveraged finance left tail stays under pressure from higher rates.

GS forecasts excess returns below post-GFC medians and recommends keeping downside protection, particularly in USD IG, where its forecasts imply negative excess returns. Its economists see downside risks to a 2.8% global growth forecast.
Wider-spread forecasts sit around the 30th to 50th percentile of post-GFC outcomes. GS frames this as a call for issuer-level dispersion, not market-wide disruption.

Risks to wider spreads: renewed geopolitical escalation, higher energy prices, a return of elevated rates volatility and larger-than-expected debt issuance. Lower energy prices, contained volatility and lighter supply would support tighter spreads.

GS keeps a modest preference for USD over EUR, stronger in IG than HY, and is neutral on USD HY vs EUR HY because meaningful risk premium is already priced. Drivers for EUR weakness are energy dependence, fiscal risk, the French presidential elections in April and May, and slowing 1Q growth.

GS expects the AI-related supply gap that weighed on USD credit to narrow in 2027 as AI issuers diversify funding across currencies, eroding part of EUR credit's technical advantage. A material fall in energy prices is the main risk to the USD-over-EUR call.

Supply: GS forecasts USD IG gross supply of $2.4 trillion and net supply of $1.15 trillion, both annual records. Drivers are AI financing, maturity walls, strategic M&A and US issuers diversifying into EUR.

GS expects USD leveraged loan issuance to stay elevated on AI financing and a possible sponsor recovery. EUR leveraged loan supply should come in slightly below 2026, and CLO gross supply should slow slightly in both USD and EUR as refinancing and reset activity is past peak.

Hyperscalers collectively reported negative free cash flow in 3Q2026, which makes debt market access a competitive advantage in the AI buildout. GS estimates nearly $700 billion of AI-related gross issuance globally year to date, of which $296 billion came from the five hyperscalers and nearly $160 billion from project financing.

GS forecasts $440 billion of direct hyperscaler debt issuance in 2027, assuming 35% of capex is debt-financed. It also forecasts $545 billion of AI-related project finance, split into $225 billion for data center shells and $320 billion for chips and compute.

Upside risks to AI supply: delayed monetization, rising purchase commitments, more capex, and saturation in corporate credit. Downside risks to project finance: construction delays, tighter financing economics, and possible data center moratoria after the midterms.

Lower AI issuance has two paths with different spread effects. Faster monetization and self-funding would be constructive for spreads. Issuer funding constraints or saturation in syndicated credit would be mixed, especially if financing moves to other structures or private markets.

27 USD IG deals of $10 billion or more have priced this year, totaling $500 billion, and 66% were AI-related. Investors demand larger new-issue concessions on AI deals than non-AI deals. GS says price alone cannot clear the market in 2027 and clarity on monetization and funding plans is needed.
GS selectively backs well-underwritten project finance, favoring offtaker quality, principal coverage and refinancing economics. It sees macro-driven widening as an entry point into such deals.

Ratings: GS moves to prefer USD IG over HY, from neutral since August 2026, citing growth downside, friendlier duration and a mature cycle. It does not expect large decompression because the USD HY/IG spread ratio is at the 83rd percentile.
In EUR, GS stays neutral between IG and HY. The EUR HY/IG ratio is at the 81st percentile and EUR HY has a higher-quality mix, with a larger BB and smaller CCC cohort.

Within IG, GS prefers BBB over AAA, AA and A in USD and EUR. AAA/AA issuers account for 22% of USD IG and 15% of EUR IG supply this year, the highest shares since 2016 and 2018, because of AI issuance concentrated among higher-rated names.

Within HY, GS prefers B over BB in USD, since BB has a record 67% of year-to-date supply and faces pressure from AI project finance. It prefers BB over B in EUR and recommends underweighting CCCs in both markets.

Sectors: AI-related vs everything else is the main differentiator. GS stays underweight Technology in IG and moves underweight USD HY Technology after revising project finance supply. Key overweights are Banks, Energy and Health Care.

GS is becoming less negative on energy-input-intensive sectors such as Airlines, Paper & Packaging and parts of Consumer Discretionary. It stays underweight rate-sensitive REITs and Autos. Energy is supported by oil above breakeven for many issuers, and Health Care by limited AI exposure.

Exhibit 11 changes include: Pharmaceuticals to OW from N in USD and EUR IG, Insurance to N from OW across markets, Utilities to UW from N in IG and N from OW in USD HY, Cable Satellite, Wireless and Wirelines to OW in USD HY, and Building Materials, Home Construction and Construction Machinery to UW.

Curves: GS thinks some back-end flattening in AI-related USD IG curves is overdone, because longer-term contingent guarantees should floor long-end spreads. Non-AI front-end curves should stay range-bound rather than flatten.

Capital structure: GS prefers moving down in capital structure over moving down in credit quality. In USD it prefers non-financial hybrids to BB HY and finds money-center bank tier 2 debt compelling. It stays cautious on EUR AT1s until a better entry point because of limited carry, tighter reset spreads and sovereign spillover risk through 1Q2027.

Duration should be friendlier in 2027 after being a headwind in 2026. GS prefers HY bonds over leveraged loans in USD and EUR on carry, quality and software loan refinancing risk. It prefers IG CLO tranches over corporate bonds on spread and mezzanine CLO tranches over leveraged loans.

Defaults: 12-month trailing rates in October were 3.2% in USD HY, 4.3% in EUR HY, 4.0% in USD leveraged loans and 2.5% in EUR leveraged loans. GS forecasts 4%, 5%, 5% and 4% respectively by year-end 2027, a modest rise. Distressed exchanges and repeat defaulters keep lowering recoveries, with senior unsecured USD HY recoveries around $30 vs roughly $40 in 2021.

Hedges: macro hedges were less useful in 2026 because risks were distributional. In 2027 the main AI risks are more likely to spill into broad macro weakness, so GS advises resetting macro hedges in periods of strength, especially into year-end. Off-the-run indices can cut carry cost but share vulnerability to AI risks.

Private credit growth areas for 2027: a sponsor activity rebound, larger private capital participation in the AI buildout (including IG private placements), and share recapture from broadly syndicated loans on Software maturity walls. 32% of US PE inventory is aged six years or more, the highest since 2000.

trade_ideas.description: Maintain macro downside protection, particularly in USD IG, and reset hedges in periods of strength into year-end
trade_ideas.rationale: Risks from AI capacity constraints or insufficient monetization are more likely to spill into broad macro weakness.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight USD IG vs EUR IG
trade_ideas.rationale: EUR faces energy, fiscal and election headwinds and a less supportive technical backdrop.
trade_ideas.risk: A material decline in energy prices would likely support EUR spreads.

trade_ideas.description: Prefer USD IG over USD HY
trade_ideas.rationale: Growth downside, friendlier duration and a mature cycle point to modest HY underperformance.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight BBB vs AAA/AA/A in USD and EUR IG
trade_ideas.rationale: Heavy AI-related debt supply from AA and higher-rated issuers.

trade_ideas.description: Prefer HY bonds over leveraged loans in USD and EUR
trade_ideas.rationale: Carry differential, superior credit quality in HY and loan refinancing risk tied to software exposure.

trade_ideas.description: Own USD non-financial hybrids over BB HY and money-center bank tier 2 subordinated debt
trade_ideas.rationale: Picks up subordination premium from higher-quality borrowers instead of moving down in credit quality.

trade_ideas.description: Own mezzanine CLO tranches over leveraged loans and IG CLO tranches over corporate bonds on spread
trade_ideas.rationale: Subordination is a buffer against sticky defaults and dispersed loan outcomes.

trade_ideas.description: Underweight CCCs in USD and EUR HY, and stay cautious on EUR AT1s
trade_ideas.rationale: Elevated refinancing costs, idiosyncratic risk, limited carry and sovereign spillover risk.

trade_ideas.description: Selective, bottom-up entry into well-underwritten AI project finance on macro-driven widening
trade_ideas.rationale: Offtaker quality, principal coverage and refinancing economics are the differentiators.
trade_ideas.risk: Construction delays, tighter financing economics and data center moratoria.

charts_described: Exhibit 3 ranks spread percentiles across global credit markets since 1/2010, with USD IG and GBP IG among the richest and EUR CCC, USD CCC and Agency MBS basis among the cheapest.

Exhibit 5 shows hyperscaler debt issuance of $108 billion in 2025, $296 billion in 2026 and a $440 billion 2027 estimate, and AI project finance of $77 billion in 2025 rising to $225 billion in 2026 and $545 billion in 2027E.
Exhibit 7 plots the USD and EUR HY/IG spread ratios, both just above the 80th percentile as of November 15, 2026.
Exhibit 9 shows the BB share of USD HY issuance at a record high.
vol_and_positioning: GS advises using periods of strength, especially into year-end, to reset macro hedges because the credit cycle is mature and the bar for growth is higher.
Off-the-run indices can reduce carry costs for hedges. Their lower AI exposure means a lower running spread, but they share similar vulnerabilities if AI risks turn into broader growth downside.
Exhibit 18 shows 3-month implied volatility on at-the-money iTraxx Main, CDX IG, iTraxx Xover and CDX HY options.
Spread percentile ranks: the USD HY/IG ratio is at the 83rd percentile and the EUR HY/IG ratio at the 81st, so HY is cheap vs IG but GS does not expect large decompression.
geopolitical: French presidential elections in April and May 2027 are a headwind for EUR credit spreads.
Renewed geopolitical escalation and higher energy prices are named as key risks to wider spreads.
Europe's greater energy dependence and fiscal risk weigh on EUR credit.
Possible data center moratoria after the US midterm elections are a downside risk to AI project finance volumes.

tension_points.bull_case: Faster monetization and greater self-funding by AI issuers would lower supply and be constructive for spreads. GS also sees macro-driven widening as an entry point into well-underwritten project finance.
tension_points.bear_case: Jumbo AI deals test market capacity and investors already demand larger concessions than on non-AI deals. Saturation in syndicated credit or issuer funding constraints would be mixed for spreads, especially if financing shifts to private markets.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Greater clarity on monetization and funding plans in 2027 is needed to keep supply clearing without weighing more heavily on spreads.

tension_points.bull_case: USD IG is favored because Europe has greater energy dependence, fiscal risk and an election calendar headwind, plus a slowing 1Q.
tension_points.bear_case: AI-related USD supply is expected to diversify into EUR, eroding EUR credit's technical advantage over USD.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A material decline in energy prices would likely support EUR spreads even with elevated political risk.

tension_points.theme: macro hedges in a mature cycle
tension_points.bull_case: Non-AI performing credit proved resilient in 2026 and growth looks more resilient, which could keep non-AI spreads range-bound.
tension_points.bear_case: A peaking AI impulse, higher rates and elevated volatility mean AI risks could spill into broad macro weakness, which makes hedges worth keeping.
